sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the Plaintiff case are that- That the plaintiff has an extent of 1 acre in S.No.112 in the schedule property of her husband, after his death at a partition amongst her sons and daughters and herself fell to her share in the suit O.S.No.453/2003 on the file of the City Civil Court, Bangalore.
This property and other properties were Cont'd..

OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO acquired by the State of Karnataka for the benefit of DRDA, Bangalore, a Central Government and after several rounds of litigation questioning the acquisition, in the Supreme Court as well, a compromise was arrived at where the terms of the compromise in CA.6362, 6363, 6364, 6365, 6366, 6367 and 6368/2001 dated 07.10.2004 was that the defense department the defendant is entitled for half the land and the remaining half should be given back to the owner i.e., 50% of the acquired land should be returned to the owner.
The defendant had taken possession to the acquisition and by virtue of the compromise, the owners became entitled for 50% of the acquired land.
This is a compromise arrived at before the Supreme Court of India.
Thus the defendant is under an obligation to return 20 guntas in S.No.112 of Benniganahalli which was also the subject matter of acquisition.

It is further stated that, the DRDO, Bangalore the beneficiary was approached by her several times to give effect to the compromise order of the Supreme Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO Court and it went on promising to do but did not do any all.

Hence, a notice dated 13.01.2017 was issued to the defendant pointing out the in action of the DRDO, Bangalore and called upon to execute the necessary deeds for giving effect to the terms of the compromise under Sec.80 of CPC.
The defendant has not replied to the said notice.
The compromise there is an obligation on the part of the defendant to return 50% of the acquired land of the plaintiff as her 1 acre is acquired.

Under Sec.39 of the Specific relief Act, the Court can compel performance of the act by means of a mandatory injunction and prevent the breach of the obligation .Hence, the Plaintiff has filed this suit.

3. In spite of service of suit summons, the defendant remained absent and hence, placed ex- parte.
4.
In order to prove the suit of the plaintiff, the GPA holder of plaintiff got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to P.11.

On the other hand defendant neither appeared before the court nor adduced any evidence and not produced any documents on her behalf.

6. Heard the arguments of the learned Counsel and perused the materials placed on record.
7.

On the basis of the above pleadings, the following points arise for consideration of this court:-
1.

Whether the Plaintiff proves that the defendant has not complied the compromise order dated 7-10-2004 in CAS 6362,6363, 6364,6365, 6466, 6367 and 6368/2001 and CA 6362/2001 before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in transferring 50% of the land in the schedule property in Sy.No.112 of Benniganahalli village ?
2. Whether the Plaintiff is entitled for the relief of mandatory injunction as sought for in the plaint?
3. What Order or decree ?

8. The findings of this court on the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 - In the Affirmative Point No.2 - In the Affirmative Point No.3 - As per final order, for the following - Cont'd..

fell to her share in the suit O.S.No.453/2003 on the file of the City Civil Court, Bangalore.

that the defendant is entitled for half the land and the remaining half should be given back to the owner i.e., 50% of the acquired land should be returned to the owner.

The defendant had taken possession pursuant Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO to the acquisition and by virtue of the compromise, the owners became entitled for 50% of the acquired land.
This is a compromise arrived at before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
Thus, the defendant is under an obligation to return 20 guntas in Sy.No.112 of Benniganahalli which was also the subject matter of acquisition.

Hence, a notice dated 13.01.2017 was issued to the defendant pointing out the inaction of the DRDO, Bangalore and called upon to execute the necessary deeds for giving effect to the terms of the compromise under Sec.80 of CPC.
The defendant has not replied to the said notice.
Under the compromise, there is an obligation on the part of the defendant to return 50% of the acquired land to the plaintiff as her 1 acre is acquired.

11. In order to prove the case of the Plaintiff, her son Sri S.Govindaraju as a GPA holder entered into Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO witness box and filed sworn affidavit in chief as PW1 and in support of her case several documents were produced and marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
Ex . P.1
is the General Power of Attorney through which plaintiff gave authority to PW.1 to prosecute the above case on her behalf.
Ex . P.2 is the certified copy of decree passed by Lok Adalath in OS.No.453/2003.
As per the terms and conditions laid down in Ex.P.2, the partition among plaintiff and her children was executed.
The 3rd item of schedule-C of Ex.P.2 is the schedule property of this suit.
The said property had fallen into the share of the plaintiff Smt.Venkatamma.

In Ex.P.3 the legal notice issued to the defendant by the plaintiff on 2-1-2017, the plaintiff made a request to comply the compromise decree as stated in the plaint and informed him that if he fails to do so, then plaintiff will proceed against defendant under law.
Ex.P.6 is the encumbrance certificate in form No.16 for the period from 1-4-2004 to 20-7-2017 in respect of suit schedule property, which shows no encumbrances pertaining to said property.
Ex.P.7 is the encumbrance certificate in Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO Form No.15 in respect of suit schedule property in the name of plaintiff, which reflects the partition dated 31-10-2003 through Lok Adalath
. Ex.P.8 is the RTC extract for the year 2001-02 in respect of Sy.No.112 which shows 2 acre 11 guntas of the land in the name of Department of Defence.

Ex.P.9 is the certified copy of Gazette notification dated 30-5-1989 published by the Government of Karnataka about acquisition of land for a public purpose to wit for DRDO Complex in favour of Defence Department Bangalore.

In serial No.64 of Ex.P.9,
there is mention about Sy.No.112 in the name of Shamanna who was the husband of this plaintiff.
It is important to note that in the said list, Sy.No.101/3 is listed in the name of M.Shamanna.

While comparing this document with Ex.P.13 that is the order dated 24-8-2000 in Writ Appeal No.2002- 2010/2000 filed by the defendants herein against the State of Karnataka along with the persons listed in Ex.P.9 as the respondents.

In the said Writ petition, the defendant herein made both Shamanna and Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO respectively.

In para No.4 of page No.12 of Ex.P.13, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that "surprisingly, the government after the order of Supreme Court denotified 44 acres and issued a notification under Section 48 of the Act in terms of Annexure H to H8 filed with this petition".

Further, in para-10 page No.15 observed that "in terms of the order of Supreme Court award has also been passed in respect of 42 acres and amounts have been deposited by the Appellant before the Spl.Land Acquisition Officer.

It is at this stage the State Government has invoked its power under Sec48 and has denotified lands in all measuring 44 acres Smt. Venkatamma vs Union Of India on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51839892/
4 as per Annexure H and H8 of the Writ Petitions.

The learned Judge, after careful consideration of materials on record in our opinion came to a right conclusion that the exercise of power under Sec.48(1) in the case on hand is malafide exercise of power We agree with the finding of the learned Judge that the State Government could not have invoked its power under Sec.48 of the Act after the order of the Supreme Court that too with a specific Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO direction for completion of acquisition proceedings as could be seen from the Order of the Supreme Court itself", and the writ petition was accepted partly.
Ex.P.10 is the certified copy of order passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India dated 7-10-2004 in Civil Appeal No.6362/2001.

In its 1st paragraph it is mentioned as "it is fit case for the parties to amicably settle the matter, by which the Union of India/DRDO will hand over possession/give up all or any claim over 50% of the total extent of the lands in the above civil appeals and the appellants would accept the same in proportion to their share and receive compensation in lieu of the remaining 50% of the lands, as per the proceedings pending under the land Acquisition Act 1894."
12.

In point No.1 in said order, it is stated as "Accordingly, the Appellants in C.A.Nos.6362, 6363,
6364, 6366 and 6367 of 2001 will obtain through their authorised representative/retain possession,
as the case may be, of the following lands representing 50% of the lands claimed by them".
Cont'd..
There is a list given in the said order as to for which of the lands in survey numbers compensation was claimed and received compensation.
In that list Sy.No.101/3 is mention but not mentioned Sy.No.112.
As discussed above, Sy.No.101/3 is in the name of M.Shamanna and Sy.No.112 is in the name of Shamanna.
That means, this plaintiff has not received any relief under Land Acquisition Act.
Ex.P.12 is the certified copy of order in W.P.No.38638-646/98 dated 25-1-2000 filed by the defendant herein against the persons listed in Ex.P.9 the government Gazette.
The said writ petition was rejected by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

In para-10 of page No.15 of the said order, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that:
"The notification letter was admittedly received by the defence Department.
After the receipt of this letter the Defence Dept., in the year 1996 itself has replied stating that they are moving the State Government not to withdraw the acquisition proceedings.
This letter conclusively shows that the Defence Dept. had the knowledge of de- notifications impugned in these petitions.

After de-notifications the land owners have sold certain bits of land in Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO favour of third parties under different registered sale deeds.
Some of the land owners have also stated that they have entered into agreements in favour of 3 rd parties.
Some of the respondents who made applications in these petitions to come on record have purchased certain lands from the land owners.

All these transactions of sale, agreements of sale are after the Smt. Venkatamma vs Union Of India on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51839892/
5 issuance of the documentary evidence-notifications and therefore, they are to be considered as bona fide transactions for valuable consideration.

sentences.text: Some of them have also developed the property after the purchase.
Under these circumstances, it is not appropriate for this court to ignore the latches on the part of the Union of India".

14. Therefore, on the basis of above discussions, the plaintiff has made out prima facie grounds in her favour as per Ex.P.14 the order of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and the Joint memo filed by the parties in C.A.Nos CAS 6362, 6363, 6364, 6365, 6466, 6367 and 6368/2001 and I A No 7 of 2004 in CA.6362/2001.
15.
On the other hand, in spite of service of suit summons, the defendant neither appeared before the court nor adduced any evidence and not produced any documents in support of defence side.

Regarding Limitation and jurisdiction etc., Ex.P 3 is the office Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO copy of legal notice dated 2-1-2017 issued by the plaintiff to the defendant, Ex.P.4 is the postal receipt and Ex.P.5 is the endorsement issued by the Department of Post, India dated 24-7-2017.
These three documents shows that the plaintiff has complied Section 80 notice as the defendant is Government authority.

As per plaint, the cause of action arose on and from the expiry of the 2months period after the knowledge of the service of the notice on the defendant that is Ex.P.3 and the suit schedule property is situated and where the DRDO of the defendant is situated within the jurisdiction of this court.

Under the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the oral and documentary evidence as discussed supra and in view of the fact that defendant has not appeared before the court and no contra evidence by the defendant, this court is of the opinion that the Plaintiff has proved that the defendant has not complied the terms and conditions of the compromise order dated 7-10-2004 in C.A.Nos.6362,
6363, 6364, 6365, 6466, 6367 and 6368/2001 and I A No.7 of 2004 Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO in CA.6362/2001 and therefore, this court is of the considered opinion that the plaintiff is entitled for 50% of the land acquired in Sy.No.112 of Benniganahalli village and the defendant is required to be directed to transfer 50% of the land in Sy.No.112 in favour of the Plaintiff by way of mandatory injunction.
Hence, this court answers answer Point Nos.1 & 2 in the 'Affirmative'.
16. Point No.3 : For the foregoing reasons and discussions and considering the findings on the above points, suit of the Plaintiff deserves to be decreed.

In the result, this Court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The suit filed by the plaintiff is hereby decreed.

The defendant is hereby directed by way of mandatory injunction, to act in terms of the compromise order dated 07.10.2004 passed in CAS Nos.6362, 6363, 6364, 6365,
6466, 6367 and 6368/2001 and CA.6362/2001 before the Hon'ble Supreme Court,
New Delhi and to transfer 50% of the land in the schedule property which is Sy.No.112 of Benniganahalli Village, in favour of the plaintiff, the subject matter of Smt. Venkatamma vs Union Of India on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51839892/
6 acquisition for the benefit of the DRDO, at Cont'd..
OS No.337/2018 OS. No.6803/2018 osoO Bangalore, within a period of two months from the date of this order.
No order as to costs.
Draw decree accordingly.
